claim: When recovery codes are written to user storage, any existing Keycloak-stored recovery-authn-codes credential is left in place, and UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to the local validator, so the old codes still work after regeneration.

The exhausted-credential cleanup calls removeStoredCredentialById on Keycloak's store using the ID of a credential that may now come from user storage (null in the reference provider), so it never removes the federated credential and can pass a null ID to the store.

Core code now parses a user-storage credential with createFromCredentialModel, which needs Keycloak-format secretData/credentialData JSON; a provider returning a plain recovery-authn-codes CredentialModel gets an unchecked exception (HTTP 500) on the login page.

The reference user storage accepts any of the 12 codes and never uses one up, so codes can be replayed without limit and the prompted code number (always #1) does not match what is validated; the new test logs in only once, so it cannot catch this.

The provider now stores recovery codes but disableCredentialType and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream handle only OTP, so user-storage recovery codes cannot be removed from the account console or admin API, and the returned credential has no id, so CredentialDeleteHelper cannot match it.
